note: THE STAGE-TEXT VOCABULARY — the wire format run-task.sh's stage() writes and
every monitoring surface parses. It used to be three independent copies (an
array in wall/server.js, a case in statusline.sh, and status.sh sourcing that
case) of a format nothing checked; this file is the one table, and the copies
are held to it by tests/stage-vocab.test.sh. docs/wall-contract.md is the prose.
The table is ORDERED for reading and DISJOINT by construction: `unless` vetoes a
match, so exactly one entry wins for any stage text and resolution never depends
on the order. Patterns are matched case-insensitively.
pattern  the stage text this entry claims
unless   a match here vetoes the entry — what keeps the table disjoint
actor    who is working: the name statusline.sh and the wall both print
key      the wall's neon signature for that actor, and its rung on FLOOR_OF
state    the wall's run state: active | alarm | ready | failed
color    statusline.sh's colour for the actor column
example  a stage string this entry must win, and no other entry may
inert    true when nothing in THIS repo emits it yet
why      a note for the row, when the row is not self-evident
Consumers: wall/server.js reads this file at startup. statusline.sh keeps
hardcoded case arms (status.sh --watch sources them) so a statusline costs no jq
on every prompt — the test is what stops them drifting. Adding a stage string to
run-task.sh means adding a row here in the same commit; the test fails until you do.

stages.why: The loudest thing on the wall: a run stopped on a human.

stages.example: review — Codex unavailable (no codex CLI on this machine) → Claude reviewer (Claude sub)
stages.why: Unanchored: the Claude tier is named mid-sentence by the fallback stage and at the head of a fix round. `unless` hands the visual rows below their own version of it.

stages.example: review failed silently — diff is unreviewed
stages.why: Written after the LAST tier gave up, so it is nobody's work in progress — and it must not read as Codex's, which Codex may never have been part of.
The greedy arm. Everything above it that starts with review/fix is vetoed here rather than by sitting earlier in the list.

stages.example: visual fix round 2 — Claude reviewer (Claude sub)

stages.why: Vetoed by Claude for the same reason the code path is: a visual fix that fell through to the Claude tier belongs to the row above.

stages.example: visual gate — rendering the shots (script, no model)
stages.why: The visual profile's render-and-grade round. Deterministic like the test gate, so it borrows the gate's neon and its rung rather than inventing a floor.

The third-vendor trajectory score. It runs on the review floor and is nobody the city has a neon for — no model of the pipeline, no decision of its own — so it borrows the neutral grey the other non-model stages use.

stages.example: test gate #2 skipped — review committed nothing
ticket sync — PR link + In Review (script — no model)

stages.why: A run that deferred itself is neither working nor finished; it keeps a live panel while it waits for its own one-shot to fire.

stages.example: base sync — merge latest main (script — no model)
sync failed: gate failed after base sync
stages.why: sync-pr.sh's failure is not a terminal `done:`, so the run stays a live panel — a loud one.

Terminal, and still an alarm: the run stopped on a human and stays pinned up until somebody answers. wall/server.js re-labels the actor to `needs input` and recovers the floor work stopped on from stages.log; the terminals hide every `done:` line, so the actor here is theirs.

Match the failure WORDS, not a whitelist of the good ones: every failing STATUS ends in _failed or is `rejected` — the visual profile's `visual_failed` included, which is why a profile can add an outcome without touching this table — while sync-pr.sh's prose `done: PR branch synced …` is a success.
Only `done: ready` pours a building into the district — that check is DONE_READY in wall/server.js, not this row, which is the broader `it finished and nothing failed`.
